**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The governing-law clause (¶p0145) applies the internal laws of the State of New York without regard to conflict-of-law principles, and the venue clause (¶p0146) requires any suit to be instituted in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the SDNY or the New York state courts, together with waivers of venue objections and forum non conveniens. This sits at the playbook's **preferred** position (New York law, exclusive New York courts), not merely the fallback.

A document-wide search for "arbitration" returned no results, so there is no mandatory arbitration and no foreign seat to assess — the walk-away scenario (vendor home jurisdiction outside the accepted list, or arbitration seated abroad) is not present.

One immaterial variance noted for the record only: venue is expressed as the "City of New York" rather than "New York County." Since the clause designates the exclusive New York state and federal courts sitting there, this is a minor sub-element short of the preferred wording and is not flagged or redlined per the classification semantics.
